articles.title: KFF Survey Shows Employer Health Insurance Premiums Surge Nearly 10%
articles.summary: A new KFF report reveals that workers are paying nearly 10% more for family health insurance premiums on employer-sponsored plans. This rising cost burden underscores the ongoing pressure on self-funded employers to manage healthcare spending and reevaluate benefit plan designs.
articles.source_line: Source: ABC News - Breaking News, Latest News and Videos; Fri, 23 Oct 2026 18:44:10 GMT
articles.source_name: ABC News - Breaking News, Latest News and Videos

articles.title: Employer-Sponsored Health Insurance Costs Continue Escalating Nationwide
articles.summary: A new nonpartisan survey reveals that the cost of employer-sponsored health plans has risen once again, putting additional financial strain on self-funded employers. Pharmacy benefits remain a major driver of these escalating healthcare costs, increasing the urgency for employers to adopt aggressive PBM cost-management and plan design strategies.

articles.title: Major Employers Sue UnitedHealth Over Alleged Bogus Health Claims
articles.summary: Kraft Heinz and Aramark have filed a lawsuit against UnitedHealth, alleging the insurer manipulated health claims and costs. This high-profile litigation highlights growing friction between self-funded employers and health plan administrators regarding claims transparency and financial accountability.

articles.title: Integrating Copay Programs and Gross-to-Net Revenue Protection Strategies
articles.summary: This Drug Channels article examines the intersection of copay assistance programs and gross-to-net revenue optimization for pharmaceutical manufacturers. While focused on manufacturer revenue strategies rather than direct self-funded employer plan design, the underlying dynamics impact specialty drug pricing and rebate structures that affect PBM economics. However, it lacks direct, actionable relevance for self-funded employer health plan cost management today.
articles.source_line: Source: Drug Channels; Fri, 23 Oct 2026 10:00:00 GMT

articles.title: Consumer Advocates Raise Concerns Over Employer-Sponsored Plan Benefit Designs
articles.summary: Consumer representatives are expressing growing concern that self-funded employer health plan designs may increasingly disadvantage sicker employees through shifting cost burdens. This trend highlights the ongoing tension between employer cost-management strategies and adequacy of coverage for high-utilization members. Self-funded plan sponsors must carefully balance affordability initiatives with equitable access to care.

articles.title: Launch Prices for New Prescription Drugs Surge 35%
articles.summary: A new report reveals that launch prices for newly approved prescription drugs surged by 35%, driving up gross drug costs for commercial plans. This steep inflation in launch pricing directly threatens the affordability of self-funded employer health plans, intensifying the need for aggressive PBM formulary management and cost containment strategies.

articles.title: First PBM Integrates Instacart Health Fresh Funds Into Employer Benefits
articles.summary: A PBM has partnered with Instacart to incorporate Fresh Funds into employee benefits, allowing self-funded employers to offer targeted grocery stipends for nutrition and health. This development highlights an expanding trend where PBMs and health plan administrators move beyond traditional pharmacy to integrate food-as-medicine initiatives into corporate wellness. For self-funded employers, this offers a novel plan design option to address chronic conditions and total healthcare cost management.
articles.source_line: Source: Progressive Grocer; Fri, 23 Oct 2026 15:00:57 GMT

articles.title: House Oversight Committee Probes PBM Independent Pharmacy Audits
articles.summary: The House Oversight Committee has launched an inquiry into pharmacy benefit managers regarding their audit practices for independent pharmacies. This congressional scrutiny adds to the growing pressure on PBM transparency, contract practices, and regulatory oversight affecting self-funded health plans.
articles.source_line: Source: Fierce Healthcare; Fri, 23 Oct 2026 19:00:00 GMT

articles.title: House Committee Launches Investigation Into Major PBMs
articles.summary: The House Oversight Committee has initiated a formal probe into the three largest pharmacy benefit managers—Optum Rx, Express Scripts, and CVS Caremark—scrutinizing their business practices and pricing models. This congressional inquiry heightens regulatory pressure on traditional PBMs, signaling potential legislative shifts that could impact how self-funded employers contract for pharmacy benefits.
articles.source_line: Source: Modern Healthcare; Fri, 23 Oct 2026 22:09:00 GMT

articles.title: Navigating Pharmacy Compliance and Legislative Impact for Self-Funded Employers
articles.summary: Mercer outlines upcoming pharmacy compliance challenges driven by recent legislative changes affecting employer-sponsored health plans. The guidance highlights how shifting regulations impact plan design, cost management, and fiduciary responsibilities for self-funded employers. Self-funded plan sponsors must closely monitor these compliance shifts to adapt their PBM strategies and avoid regulatory pitfalls.

articles.title: Employers Health Partners With Archimedes to Cut Pharmacy Costs
articles.summary: Employer coalition Employers Health has selected PBM Archimedes to provide cost-reduction strategies and alternative pharmacy benefit solutions for its members. This move highlights growing demand among employer groups for specialized PBM alternatives aimed at driving down self-funded drug spend. The partnership underscores competitive pressures in the PBM market as coalitions seek greater transparency and savings.
articles.source_line: Source: Business Wire; Fri, 23 Oct 2026 14:00:00 GMT

articles.title: Epic Systems Launches Prescription Marketplace to Enhance Price Transparency
articles.summary: Epic Systems has introduced a new prescription marketplace aimed at providing greater price transparency and lowering drug costs for patients and healthcare providers. For self-funded employers and PBMs, this technology could disrupt traditional pharmacy benefit navigation by exposing real-time drug pricing at the point of care. The development highlights increasing industry pressure for end-to-end transparency in prescription drug costs.
articles.source_line: Source: The American Action Forum; Fri, 23 Oct 2026 13:57:24 GMT

articles.title: Samsung Bioepis Report Emphasizes Biosimilar Supply Continuity for Payers
articles.summary: Samsung Bioepis released its Q4 2026 market report highlighting the critical role of supply chain reliability in biosimilar adoption. For self-funded employers and PBMs, ensuring consistent supply is essential to capturing projected cost savings from complex biologic alternatives. The report underscores that formulary design must account for both price and manufacturer stability to avoid disruption in patient care.

articles.title: Major Companies Pledge Faster Electronic Prior Authorizations
articles.summary: Five major healthcare companies have committed to streamlining and accelerating prior authorization processes using electronic standards. This shift aims to reduce administrative friction and care delays, directly impacting specialty drug management and utilization review workflows for employer-sponsored plans.
articles.source_line: Source: Healthcare Dive; Fri, 23 Oct 2026 15:54:28 GMT

articles.title: HRSA Revisits 340B Rebate Model with New Pilot Proposal
articles.summary: HRSA is exploring a new pilot proposal regarding the 340B rebate model, which could impact drug pricing and distribution dynamics. This regulatory shift is crucial for PBMs and self-funded employers monitoring 340B program integrity and specialty drug cost trends.
articles.source_line: Source: Norton Rose Fulbright; Fri, 23 Oct 2026 09:14:53 GMT

articles.title: Texas Employers Lose $353M Annually Due to 340B Program Expansion
articles.summary: A new report reveals that Texas employers absorb $353 million in annual costs as the 340B drug discount program expands with minimal transparency. This financial impact underscores the ongoing cost burden placed on self-funded health plans by complex drug pricing and distribution loopholes. The findings highlight the critical need for employer advocacy and greater transparency in pharmacy benefit operations.
articles.source_line: Source: The Business Journals; Fri, 23 Oct 2026 20:08:00 GMT

articles.title: House Panel Targets Major PBMs in Ongoing Drug Pricing Investigation
articles.summary: A new congressional investigation has been launched targeting the largest PBMs—CVS Caremark, Express Scripts, and Optum Rx—over their business practices and drug pricing models. This regulatory scrutiny increases pressure on traditional PBM transparency and could accelerate legislative reforms affecting self-funded employer health plans.
articles.source_line: Source: Seeking Alpha; Fri, 23 Oct 2026 16:14:33 GMT
